# AWS Serverless Metadata Workflow

> A public, deployable, and tested reconstruction of the AWS serverless metadata workflow Bradley Matera built during an AWS Support Engineering internship.

Canonical site: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/
Repository: https://github.com/BradleyMatera/Office
Recruiter portfolio: https://bradleymatera.dev/recruiter/
AWS writing hub: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/writing.html
Proof map: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/proof.html
Verified AWS sources: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/sources.html
Design system: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/design-system.html

## Core architecture

1. An object is uploaded under a configured Amazon S3 key prefix, defaulting to `incoming/`.
2. S3 sends an object-created notification to AWS Lambda.
3. The Python 3.12 function URL-decodes the key and uses `HeadObject` to read object metadata without downloading the body.
4. It normalizes metadata into a documented versioned schema.
5. It derives a deterministic SHA-256 `RecordId` from the bucket, decoded key, version ID, and ETag.
6. It writes to DynamoDB with `attribute_not_exists(RecordId)` so repeated event delivery is idempotent.
7. Unexpected failures are raised for Lambda asynchronous retry.
8. Events that still fail are sent to an encrypted SQS failure queue.
9. CloudWatch alarms cover Lambda errors, Lambda throttles, and visible failed events. Optional SNS email alerts require subscription confirmation.

## Verified implementation facts

- Python unit tests: 11 passing in the August 3, 2026 local audit.
- Statement and branch coverage: 100% in that audit.
- Infrastructure: AWS SAM and CloudFormation.
- Storage protections: S3 encryption, versioning, ACLs disabled, Block Public Access enabled.
- Database protections: DynamoDB encryption, on-demand billing, point-in-time recovery, retained data policy.
- Failure handling: maximum event age, two asynchronous retries, encrypted SQS on-failure destination.
- Site: static GitHub Pages, no runtime AWS credentials, no direct bucket or table access.

## Internship scope

The internship work was completed in isolated training and project environments. The public repository does not claim:

- production customer ownership
- live enterprise ticket ownership
- unrestricted Amazon administrative access
- that the public files are exact confidential internship source files
- that a live AWS stack is currently deployed in Bradley Matera's account

## Best public description

Bradley Matera built an event-driven AWS metadata workflow during an AWS Support Engineering internship using S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, and a static frontend layer. He created a measurable usage-based cost model and later reconstructed the system publicly with AWS SAM, idempotent writes, retries, a failure queue, monitoring, tests, security controls, diagrams, verified official AWS sources, and full technical documentation.
